You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no body and are never drawn. Describe only the shared place, weather and light. Where the section shows one of them, its presence may appear only as smoke, cloud, fire, wind or light spread through the place. Never describe its throne, seat, chariot, robe, train, face, hands, hair, body or silhouette, even as an empty seat, a denial or a figure made of light: bodily words in the text are metaphors. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them. The cast list covers the whole section; do not force every cast member into the shared setting or add individual poses, actions or moments.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return. People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples. Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor. Buildings and objects: Villages, palaces, temples, city gates and exile settlements.

- Draw one scene at one instant: no collage and no sequence of steps. If the moment recounts several actions, pick one representative instant. If it has no event (a list, law, saying or greeting), illustrate its content or setting.
- Show what the moment is about. When the moment is mostly someone's words (a prophecy, oracle, poem, proverb, prayer, letter, argument or teaching, or a story, parable, vision or memory being told), draw what the words describe and leave the speaker, writer and listeners out, unless the text shows them inside that scene (a visionary within the vision). Never put a speaker, writer or listener into a scene their words only describe, and never make them a figure of their own words, such as the king ready for battle or the man standing in the gap.
- In `selectedCast`, list every section cast entry that will be visible: people, groups, places, objects, and any presence without form shown through its effects. Give a few words of the text for each. Leave out cast who are elsewhere or only mentioned. Anyone without a cast entry may appear as an unnamed role or crowd when the moment needs them.
- Describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Leave fixed appearance to canon, name no art style, and put no text or writing in the scene. Keep every depiction rule.
- The scene fields carry this moment's place, time, light and situational clothing. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is a suggestion for them: keep what fits this moment and change what does not. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when given instead, are binding: keep the setting and time of day consistent with them.
- Each field is one or two short phrases.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Creation and the patriarchs. People: Ancient Near Eastern households, herders and farmers. Dress: Simple wool or linen wraps, tunics and sandals. Technology: Hand tools, herding, farming and weighed metal; no modern objects.
STORY SECTION: Isaac sends Jacob to Paddan Aram

MOMENT (Genesis 28:6): Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan Aram, to take him a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he gave him a command, saying, “You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;”
PREVIOUS: Isaac sent Jacob away. He went to Paddan Aram to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.
NEXT: and that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Paddan Aram.

CAST ON STAGE IN THIS SECTION (id: name):
- isaac_son_of_abraham_and_sarah: Isaac, son of Abraham and Sarah
- jacob: Jacob
- esau: Esau

SECTION LOOK GUIDE (a suggestion; keep what fits this moment):

A PREVIOUS PLAN FOR THIS MOMENT WAS REJECTED. Write a new plan that fixes every problem below and keeps what was correct:
- canon_conflict: Isaac's fixed canon gives him a late-youth to middle-age build and face, but the scene field depicts him as aged. (plan said: "Isaac, aged")

focusQuote.description: A few words copied from MOMENT naming what this image shows.

instant.description: One sentence fixing the single instant to draw: who is where, doing what.

evidence.description: A few words from the text that put this entry in the scene.

primarySubject.description: The main subject and its pose or placement at that instant. One or two short phrases.

action.description: What happens at that one instant. One or two short phrases.

setting.description: The physical place and surroundings, consistent with the text and era. One or two short phrases.

secondaryElements.description: Supporting people, props and effects with their placement. One or two short phrases.

mood.description: The emotional atmosphere of the moment. One or two short phrases.

timeOfDay.description: This moment's time of day, weather and situational light. One or two short phrases.

composition.description: Viewpoint, framing and placement of the subjects, independent of art style. One or two short phrases.

messages.content:
You check an illustration plan before it is drawn. You get the moment's text with its neighbours, the depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm), the plan's selected cast ids (`present`), its seven scene fields, any OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS that rendering will use, and the canon of the selected entries. Report only clear problems that a careful reader would agree with, and return an empty list when the plan is a reasonable illustration of the moment. Do not report preferences, small omissions or other valid readings. Return only JSON.
The text decides who is in the scene; canon decides how they look; the scene plan decides this moment's place, time, light, clothing and action. Owner look constraints, when given, are binding.
Kinds:
- unselected_figure: a section cast entry (a person, group, place, object, or a no-form presence shown as its effect) is clearly depicted in a scene field but its id is not in present. Use its id.
- outside_instant: a selected or described person or presence does not belong in this moment, such as a speaker, writer, prophet or listener put into a scene their words only describe or made a figure of their own words, the narrator of a story or vision, someone from a different event, or a no-form presence the moment does not show. Use its id, or empty.
- not_one_instant: the fields give someone incompatible poses or places, or show successive steps as one image.
- embodied_formless: a hasForm false entry is given a body, face, hands, clothing, a robe or train, a silhouette, a throne or seat of its own, or is described as seated or standing.
- look_conflict: an OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS value (only when supplied) contradicts the scene, the text or the depiction rules. Quote that value.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts a selected entry's fixed canon. Quote the scene field.
- missing_canon: the scene depicts a named recurring character or group with no section cast entry. Leave entryId empty.
For each problem, copy a short exact phrase from a scene field or a selected id into planQuote (from an owner constraint for look_conflict) and give a one-sentence reason.

DEPICTION RULES
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
STORY SECTION: Isaac sends Jacob to Paddan Aram

MOMENT (Genesis 28:6): Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan Aram, to take him a wife from there, and that as he blessed him he gave him a command, saying, “You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;”
PREVIOUS: Isaac sent Jacob away. He went to Paddan Aram to Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob’s and Esau’s mother.
NEXT: and that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Paddan Aram.

SECTION CAST (id: name, hasForm):
- isaac_son_of_abraham_and_sarah: Isaac, son of Abraham and Sarah (hasForm: true)
- jacob: Jacob (hasForm: true)
- esau: Esau (hasForm: true)

SELECTED CANON (complete assigned stages; fixed identity, not source evidence):
- isaac_son_of_abraham_and_sarah (stage: isaac-main, kind: character, hasForm: true): Isaac: a young man in late youth to middle age; lean, sturdy build from herding and labour in the open country; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut close at the neck, short beard kept trim; calm, steady face with heavy-lidded, grey-brown eyes that grow dim with age; wears a plain undyed linen tunic with a woollen wrap of earth-brown ochre, and leather sandals; carries a wooden staff of plain olive wood, and a bundle of kindling when bound to the wood at Moriah.
- jacob (stage: jacob-main, kind: character, hasForm: true): Jacob: a slender, wiry man of middle to later years in his prime and sixties-to-seventies in old age; lean, sinewy build from long herding; smooth, unhairy skin browned by sun; dark, close-cropped hair and short beard kept trim; alert, thoughtful eyes and a clean, quiet face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and wool wrap cloak in earth brown, with leather sandals. Carries a shepherd's staff.
- esau (stage: esau-main, kind: character, hasForm: true): Esau: man of about forty to sixty, broad-shouldered and weathered from the field; ruddy, sun-darkened skin; thick dark-red hair and a full reddish beard; hairy forearms and hands; heavy brow and steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: a sleeveless wool tunic in rust-brown over a linen wrap, with a dun cloak and leather sandals.

PLAN
present: isaac_son_of_abraham_and_sarah, jacob, esau
primarySubject: Isaac standing at his tent opening, one hand raised in blessing toward Jacob kneeling before him.
action: Isaac speaks the blessing and command while Jacob bows with a staff and traveling cloak at his side.
setting: Semi-arid highland camp of goatskin tents beside a well, wild land and mud-brick town edges in the distance.
secondaryElements: Esau stands apart near the edge of the camp, watching with a hunter's bow and sheltered posture; a few household members and herd animals hold back at a respectful distance.
mood: Solemn, weighty and quietly tense, with a hint of unresolved rivalry.
timeOfDay: Late afternoon sliding toward dusk, clear dry sky with a light wind.
composition: Medium-wide view from slightly below, Isaac and Jacob centered near the tent, Esau placed off to one side in the middle distance.
